title: Marcus Smart suspended 3 games for throwing punch at Warriors player
content:
Houston Rockets guard Marcus Smart was suspended 3 games by the NBA for “throwing a punch that made contact with the face” of Golden State Warriors big man Charles Bassey, the league announced Thursday.

Smart was assessed a Flagrant 2 foul and ejected with 21 seconds remaining in the third quarter of Houston’s 115-108 win over the Warriors. The 32-year-old Smart got tangled up with Bassey on one end of the floor, and the two went face-to-face while running back to the other end. Smart threw a punch that grazed Bassey’s nose before the two were separated. He immediately walked off the floor and into the tunnel before the officials rendered a verdict.

“(Smart) said they got wrapped up and (Smart)’s elbow that he hurt got bent up,” Rockets coach Ime Udoka said after Wednesday’s win. “So, he said something to him. Bassey said, ‘What are you going to do?’ And he did it.”

When asked postgame about the altercation, Bassey said he wasn’t surprised by the reaction because Smart was showing “fake toughness.”

“I baited for him to do something,” Bassey said. “I don’t think he was trying to play. I think he was trying to get himself out of the game. … I think he was trying to chill; he wasn’t trying to hoop. Like I said, man, that was fake. Fake toughness.”

Smart will serve the suspension beginning Friday, when the Rockets host the Utah Jazz. He will also miss upcoming games against the Washington Wizards (Sunday) and Miami Heat (Monday).

The 13-year veteran has been a strong addition to the Rockets bench after signing a two-year, $13 million deal last summer to reunite with Udoka, who coached Smart with the Boston Celtics in the 2021-22 season.

Through his first nine games (one start) with Houston, Smart is averaging 8.3 points, 2.6 rebounds and two assists while shooting 43.9 percent from the field and 40 percent on 3s.
